_comment: A compiler artifact — an ABI and the creation code compiled from the same
source — in the shape Foundry writes one. It is what proves `endor-cli abi`
generates a `deploy`, in `just codegen-check` and against a real EVM in
The bytecode is `backend/anvil`'s answer contract, whose runtime returns the
word 42 for any calldata: `600a600c600039600a6000f3` copies the 10 runtime
bytes at offset 12 and returns them. It has no constructor of its own, which
is exactly why the declared one is safe — a constructor's arguments are
appended behind the creation code, and this code stops before it reads them.
So a deployment that encodes `_initial` wrongly still deploys, and it is
`answer()` coming back as 42 that says the SDK reached a contract at all.
